## Command Details

```text
Prepare governed release candidates (F053 T1).
A candidate immutably binds one exact Change (commit + committed Artifact
revisions), recorded Evidence, per-axis Review findings (logic, security,
spec compliance — Evidence references, never approvals), the target
environment, a versioned release Policy artifact, one registered F052
Runner capability pin, the credentials class, and a rollback plan into a
canonical releaseHash. Preparation is a governance write: it never deploys
and touches no git state; any drift invalidates downstream authorization.

Subcommands:
  prepare --id <release-id> --commit <40-hex> --change-artifact <type>:<identity>@<rev>
        [--change-artifact ...] --evidence-item <evidence-id> [--evidence-item ...]
        --review-logic <evidence-id> --review-security <evidence-id>
        --review-spec <evidence-id> --environment <development|staging|production>
        --release-policy <identity>@<rev> --runner <runner-id> --runner-version <v>
        --capability <name> --capability-version <v> --credential <none|scoped>
        --rollback <evidence-id>
  authorize --id <release-id>
        staging: --approval <id> --decision-identity <identity> --body <markdown>
        [--trace decides:<type>:<identity>] [--scope <scope>] --rehearsal <evidence-id>
        production: --branch-protection <evidence-id> --code-owner <identity>@<rev>
        --release-manager <identity>@<rev> --release-gate-index <n>
        --environment-gate-index <n>
  deploy --id <release-id> --request-hash <sha256:...>
  rollback --id <release-id> --request-hash <sha256:...>
  transactions [--id <release-id>]
  status --id <release-id>
  receipts --id <release-id>
  show --id <release-id>
  list [--environment <env>]

Examples:
  amber release prepare --target . --id release/web-42 --commit <40-hex> --change-artifact spec:spec/login@2 --evidence-item evidence/test-run --review-logic evidence/review-logic --review-security evidence/review-security --review-spec evidence/review-spec --environment staging --release-policy policy/release@1 --runner runner/ci --runner-version 1.0.0 --capability deploy.staging-web --capability-version 1 --credential scoped --rollback evidence/rollback-plan --json
  amber release show --target . --id release/web-42 --json
```

## Boundaries & Safety

- `--target <path>` selects repository state. Amber confines these target-relative paths, refusing `..` and symlink escapes before reading or writing: plan and scaffold destinations (including `accept --plan`), memory and context payloads, harness inputs, adapter allow-lists, workflow reports and their output directory, ledger exports, execution readiness plans, session and worktree state, governance report output, wiki export and handoff bundle output directories.
- Path validation is not OS sandboxing, and the confinement above covers only the surfaces it names, and a confined flag still accepts an absolute destination only when it stays inside the target. `governance audit --output`, `governance readiness --output`, `security audit --output`, `loop record --output`, and `explain --markdown` resolve against the working directory instead of `--target`. A path flag not listed here is confined only when the command that reads it routes through the boundary. A governed or verification command still runs with your user's file permissions.
- `wiki export`, `handoff bundle`, `workflow assess` and `governance report` reject output destinations that resolve to the target root, including `.`, an absolute root path, `nested/..`, and symlink or junction aliases of the root. Output subdirectories and defaults are unchanged.
- `wiki export` and `handoff bundle` check all planned file destinations and their parent directories before the first write, including copied wiki pages and optional replay files. An existing child symlink or junction outside the target refuses the export without changing output files. Concurrent link replacement is not prevented.
- A planned output file that shares its bytes with another name — a hard link, or a link to one — is refused before the write by `wiki export`, `handoff bundle`, `workflow assess --output-dir` and `governance report --output`, even when both names stay inside the target. A link to a single in-target file is still written through, so it replaces that file's bytes.
- `handoff validate --bundle-dir .` and `workflow assess --handoff-bundle-dir .` still accept root-level bundles as read-only inputs. Explicit handoff validation paths outside `--target` are refused.
- **Fail-Closed Behavior**: Corrupt governance state or invalid schema parameters immediately halt execution with non-zero exit codes.
